idea-plugin.name: Peephole
idea-plugin.description:
See your Android app's network traffic live, in its own tool window, not in logcat. Works with OkHttp (including Retrofit and Apollo Kotlin) and Ktor.

Features

  • REST: method, URL, status, timing, size, headers and bodies.
  • GraphQL: queries, mutations and subscriptions are detected and listed by operation name, with a GraphQL tab showing the formatted query and its variables.
  • WebSocket: every sent and received message per connection, including GraphQL-over-WebSocket and SignalR (record-separated JSON is split and formatted).
  • Readable bodies: JSON and GraphQL are pretty-printed and syntax-highlighted, with collapsible blocks and Expand All / Collapse All.
  • Copy anything: the body, the full request or response (start line, headers and body), the URL, or the request as a cURL command.
  • Multiple devices and apps: pick any connected device and any running process that uses the library.
  • Filters by type (REST / GraphQL / WebSocket), status and text; pause recording; clear; follow new calls automatically.
  • Export to HAR to open the capture in Chrome DevTools, Charles or Proxyman.
  • Production-safe: no-op artifacts for release builds, and header redaction (e.g. Authorization).
  • Logcat stays clean: traffic travels over a dedicated adb-forwarded socket.

Getting started

  1. Add the libraries to your app's build.gradle.kts: 
    debugImplementation("np.com.manjultamrakar:peephole-okhttp:0.1.0")
releaseImplementation("np.com.manjultamrakar:peephole-okhttp-noop:0.1.0")

// Ktor:
debugImplementation("np.com.manjultamrakar:peephole-ktor:0.1.0")
releaseImplementation("np.com.manjultamrakar:peephole-ktor-noop:0.1.0")
  2. Hook up your client: 
    // OkHttp / Retrofit / Apollo
OkHttpClient.Builder().addInterceptor(PeepholeInterceptor()).build()
// OkHttp WebSockets
PeepholeWebSocketFactory(client).newWebSocket(request, listener)

// Ktor
HttpClient(CIO) { install(PeepholePlugin) }
    The library starts by itself; no Application code is needed. If you use Ktor with the OkHttp engine, install only PeepholePlugin.
  3. Run a debug build on a device or emulator connected over adb.
  4. Open View | Tool Windows | Peephole, choose the Device and the App at the top, and make some requests. Calls appear as they happen.
Options such as body size limits and header redaction live in Peephole.init(context, PeepholeConfig(...)); the adb path is under Settings | Tools | Peephole.
